QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_44

question.text: If the 95% one-month VaR of an AIF is INR 2 crore, the correct interpretation is:

answer.text: There is a 95% probability the fund will not lose more than INR 2 crore over the next month
The fund is guaranteed to lose INR 2 crore
The fund's NAV will grow by INR 2 crore
The fund's management fee will be INR 2 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.9.3: A 95% one-month VaR of INR 2 crore means there is a 95% probability that the fund will NOT lose more than INR 2 crore over the next month. Equivalently, there is a 5% chance of losing more than INR 2 crore. The Trap: Option B confuses probability with certainty; VaR is a probabilistic estimate, not a guarantee. Options C and D describe entirely unrelated metrics (NAV growth and management fee). Note: VaR is a probability-based loss threshold; it does not indicate the magnitude of loss in the tail beyond the confidence level.
